nodes.title: Prime factors of the primitive parts of the denominator indices

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the factorial $n!$ lies in the subgroup of the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Q}^\times$ generated by the Fibonacci numbers $F_m$ with $m \ge 1$ if and only if $n \le 36$.
nodes.title: The largest factorial that is a Fibonacci integer is $36!$

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci cyclotomic value $\Phi_2 = \prod_{d \mid 2} F_{2/d}^{\mu(d)} = F_2 / F_1$, where $F_k$ is the $k$-th Fibonacci number and $\mu$ is the Möbius function, equals $1$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci cyclotomic value at $2$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, $\Phi_m$ is the rational number $\prod_{d \mid m} F_{m/d}^{\mu(d)}$, where $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $m$, $F_k$ is the $k$-th Fibonacci number and $\mu$ is the Möbius function. For $m > 1$ this is the value $\Phi_m(\alpha, \beta)$ of the homogenized $m$-th cyclotomic polynomial at the roots $\alpha, \beta$ of $x^2 - x - 1$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci cyclotomic values

nodes.summary: The least $m > 0$ such that $5$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_m$ is $5$, that is, the Fibonacci entry point of $5$ is $z(5) = 5$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci entry point of $5$

nodes.summary: The least $m > 0$ such that $2$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_m$ is $3$, that is, the Fibonacci entry point of $2$ is $z(2) = 3$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci entry point of $2$

nodes.summary: The entry point (rank of apparition) $z(k)$ of a natural number $k$ is the least $m > 0$ such that $k$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_m$, and $z(k) = 0$ if there is no such $m$.
nodes.title: Entry point in the Fibonacci sequence

nodes.summary: The primitive part of the Fibonacci number $F_6$ is $\Psi_6 = 1$: $F_6 = 8 = 2^3$ and the Fibonacci entry point of $2$ is $z(2) = 3 \ne 6$, so $F_6$ has no prime factor $p$ with $z(p) = 6$.
nodes.title: Primitive part of $F_6$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, the primitive part of the Fibonacci number $F_m$ is $\Psi_m = \prod_p p^{a_p}$, where the product runs over the primes $p$ dividing $F_m$ whose Fibonacci entry point is $z(p) = m$, and $a_p$ is the exponent of $p$ in $F_m$.
nodes.title: Primitive part of a Fibonacci number

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$-th Fibonacci number. For every natural number $m > 12$, every primitive prime divisor $p$ of $F_m$ (a prime $p$ that divides $F_m$ but divides no $F_n$ with $0 < n < m$) satisfies $p \equiv \pm 1 \pmod{m}$, that is, $p \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ or $p + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{m}$.
nodes.title: Carmichael's congruence for primitive prime divisors of Fibonacci numbers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
